Hi Sara / Eli —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Two quick recaps and a proposed validation plan so we can get aligned on the unit economics and next tests: 

Quick recap from demo:
- Your workload: multi-turn customer support with ~1.5k token average session, many repeated prefixes (knowledge base + customer profile) across sessions.
- Goal: validate 1) per-1M token baseline across models, 2) realistic cost delta with KV/prefix caching & batching, 3) latency SLOs at your concurrency.

Initial high-level numbers (for alignment only):
- Redwood hosted (rw-llama-70b q4): ~$17–20 per 1M tokens at observed batching and 60% cache hit assumptions.
- Hyperscaler A (managed endpoint): ~$38–45 per 1M tokens for similar throughput.
- Hyperscaler B (research endpoint): ~$32–40 per 1M tokens depending on model variant.

These are ballpark — the real delta depends on: average sequence length distribution, batching opportunity (how many simultaneous small requests we can pack), and KV cache hit rate on your recurring prefixes.

Proposed validation tests (attached plan + sample prompts):
1) Cold 1M-token throughput run (no KV cache warm) — measures raw per-token runtime cost.
2) Warmed 1M-token run after seeding prefixes (simulate 60–80% cache hit) — measures effective unit cost with caching.
3) High-concurrency micro-infer test (many 1–2k token sessions) to stress batching and latency tail.

Can you confirm: 1) an example day of traffic (session counts, avg tokens/session), and 2) whether you can provide a small sample of real session IDs/prompts (we’ll treat data confidentially) so we can run a faithful warm-run?

Attached: DN_validation_plan_v1.pdf (test matrix) and sample_prompts.jsonl (anonymized prompt set).

If that sounds good I’ll loop in engineering to pin expected numbers and schedule the runs next week.

Quick draft math and scenarios (very conservative):

Assumptions (example):
- Base runtime cost (Redwood hosted) for model X: $0.000018 per token (this maps to ~$18 per 1M tokens) for a mixed-sequence optimized config.
- Hyperscaler A managed endpoint: $0.000038/token (~$38 per 1M). Hyperscaler B: $0.000034/token (~$34 per 1M).

Cache impact: a KV/prefix cache that saves repeated prefix decoding typically reduces billable tokens only if we avoid re-sending prefix tokens to the model. For DataNimble workloads we often see 45–70% effective token reduction in warm flows. Example:
- Cold run (0% hit): Redwood $18 / 1M tokens.
- Warm run (60% hit, same # of logical responses): effective billed tokens drop by ~40% -> effective cost ~$10.8 / 1M tokens.

Batching impact: microflows (200–400 token requests) benefit from packing into larger minibatches. We model that as a throughput multiplier that lowers per-token GPU-time by ~15–25% depending on concurrency. So short flows + high concurrency + aggressive batching -> another ~20% reduction on top of caching in good cases.

Reserved capacity pricing: rough sketch for DN-481 (subject to legal/ops):
- 12m reserved GPU throughput contract: 25% discount vs payg baseline for committed capacity; 35% discount if >12 months + minimum commit.
- We can offer a trial reserved window (30 days) with credits back if they convert to full reserved contract.

I’ll attach the modeling sheet (per_token_modeling.xlsx) with scenario calc. Marcus — any technical caveats? Naomi — what should we ask DN to measure on their side to validate?

—Ben

Thanks everyone — a few technical clarifications and a recommended test schedule so DataNimble can get results that map directly to our accounting: 

How we measure cache hit rate: 
- Runtime emits a per-request trace (x-request-id) that includes: cache_lookup_count, cache_hit_count, cached_prefix_tokens_saved. We can export these traces to the console or a short CSV during the run.
- Effective billed tokens = billed_input_tokens + billed_output_tokens - cached_prefix_tokens_saved (our billing hook subtracts saved tokens for warm prefixes).

Recommended bench runs (we should run these in order so DN sees delta):
A) Cold baseline: 200k sessions worth of requests (no prefix seeding) — measure raw per-token cost.
B) Seeded warm-run: replay sample_prompts.jsonl to pre-populate KV cache; then run 1M tokens worth of traffic from live-like traces; measure cache_hit_count and cached_tokens_saved.
C) Microflow batching test: 1M tokens consisting of 60% short microflows (200–400 tokens) at peak concurrency 300 qps, measure effective batching rate and p50/p95 latency.

Instrumentation for DN: please capture (per request) the request_id and we’ll return a CSV of cache_hit_count + cached_tokens_saved. Naomi: request your tracing snippet and the token-accounting flag for their engineers.

Scheduling: we have a 2-hour window on Mon 12 Apr 2027 for environment prep; propose running A–C Tues/Wed next week. Sara/Eli — can you confirm availability?

If accepted, I’ll kick off the runs and share raw traces + per_token_modeling.xlsx updates that fold in the actual observed hit rates.
